__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus that scrapes spark-dash agents.

panels.title: Nodes up
panels.description: Agents that produced a snapshot on the last scrape.

panels.title: Not healthy
panels.description: Nodes reporting anything other than `good`. One series per state, so this counts rather than decodes.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description:
DECODE tokens/sec across every runtime — what the model is producing.

Prefill is deliberately excluded. The combined figure was measured at 47,672 tok/s on this cluster while the model generated 48: a large prompt landing inside one poll window really is that fast to ingest, and it is not what a throughput number means.

ONE sum over a name regex, not a sum per engine added together: binary `+` keeps only label sets present on both sides, so adding them returns nothing for a node running only one engine.

panels.title: Models resident
panels.description: llama.cpp models with weights in memory. Sleeping models are excluded — they hold a process but not the weights.

panels.title: Watched links down
panels.description: Down links that are still watched. Excluded interfaces are subtracted, not filtered in — a missing `monitored` flag leaves the link counted rather than silently dropped.

targets.expr: count(sparkdash_network_up{node=~"$node"} == 0 unless on (node, interface) sparkdash_network_monitored == 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Unmonitored runtimes
panels.description: An inference runtime is holding GPU memory with nothing configured to collect from it — throughput, queue depth and cache data are not reaching anything.

panels.title: GPU utilization
panels.description: NVML's utilization: the fraction of time at least one kernel was resident. It says the GPU was busy, not how well it was being used — a single small kernel reads 100%.

panels.title: GPU temperature
panels.description: The bands are METRICS, not hardcoded numbers — the agent derives them from NVML's own slowdown threshold, so they follow the silicon instead of a guess in a config file.

panels.title: SM clock vs target
panels.description: Compared against the APPLICATIONS clock, not the boost ceiling. On GB10 the ceiling (3003MHz) is never approached and the observed range brackets the applications clock (2418MHz), so calibrating against the ceiling reads as permanent throttling.

panels.title: GPU power
panels.description: Board power draw. On GB10 this is the whole module, so it moves with CPU work too rather than tracking GPU load alone.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: GB10 has NO separate VRAM. This one pool is shared by the models, every other GPU workload and the OS, which is why NVML's own memory numbers are not used anywhere.

panels.title: Memory pressure (PSI)
panels.description: SOME means at least one task stalled waiting on memory, which a busy inference box does routinely. FULL means every runnable task stalled — nothing progressed at all. On a node whose whole job is holding models in one pool, that is the difference between working hard and stopped.

panels.title: What is eating the pool
panels.description: REPEATED PER NODE deliberately. Summing this across nodes would add together pools that are physically separate, describing capacity that does not exist. Aggregated by runtime rather than per-pid, which is a cardinality trade: the per-process detail lives in the agent's live snapshot, not here.

panels.title: Tokens/sec by model
panels.description: llama.cpp throughput is a GAUGE the agent computed over its own poll, not a counter — so rate() over a window of your choosing is not available for it. vLLM and SGLang are scraped natively, so their raw counters are in this same Prometheus if you want them.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Summed per node across every engine. Waiting climbing while running is flat is a queue forming — the signal that a node is saturated rather than merely busy.

panels.title: KV cache
panels.description: vLLM and llama.cpp only. SGLang is deliberately absent: it publishes cache_hit_rate, which is the fraction of prompt tokens served from the PREFIX cache — a different question with the same 0-1 shape. 93% prefix hits is a node doing well; 93% occupancy is a node about to evict.

panels.title: Model states
panels.description: One series per state rather than an encoded enum, so this is a filter rather than a decoder ring.

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description: Bits, not bytes: network gear is rated in bits and the whole point is comparing against a 200 Gb/s link. These series are named _total and monotonic but are TYPED as gauges, so Grafana will not suggest rate() for them — it is still correct to use.

panels.title: Interfaces
panels.description: `monitored` is the exclusion set by cluster.yml. An excluded interface is still collected and still charted — only alerting ignores it.

panels.title: Snapshot age
panels.description: How stale the snapshot being served is. Climbing means collection is falling behind the poll, which presents as a dashboard that looks fine and is quietly out of date.

panels.title: Collection duration
panels.description: Wall time of one snapshot. Every runtime HTTP call shares a single wall-clock budget, so this is bounded by design rather than growing with the number of endpoints a node serves — which is what once took the agent off the dashboard entirely.

panels.title: Agent build
panels.description: A node left behind by a rollout presents as a MISSING FEATURE rather than as a stale agent — which has cost real debugging time here more than once.

panels.title: Collector errors
panels.description: Empty is the healthy state. Collectors are independent, so one failing does not stop the rest — and would otherwise be invisible.
